title: China proposes licensing limits on exports of advanced AI technology
dek: Draft rules distinguish overseas access to Chinese AI services from exporting underlying models, data and know-how.
evidence: Reuters analysis of draft Chinese regulations; not final law
takeaway: Evaluate portability of model weights, hosting rights and know-how transfers separately from ordinary API availability.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Chinese labs can offer models globally while governments separately regulate exports of technology, know-how and model deployment artifacts.

paragraphs: Compute restrictions cut both ways: Chinese labs can offer models globally while governments separately regulate exports of technology, know-how and model deployment artifacts.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: China proposed licensing for selected AI technology exports while generally exempting use through hosted APIs, apps and SaaS.
Reuters reports 23 AI-related technologies in draft controls, including advanced models, autonomous agents and large compute systems, with threshold-based coverage.

paragraphs: Hosted access versus transfer: China proposed licensing for selected AI technology exports while generally exempting use through hosted APIs, apps and SaaS.
Broader scope: Reuters reports 23 AI-related technologies in draft controls, including advanced models, autonomous agents and large compute systems, with threshold-based coverage.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: The rules were under consultation through November 15. Definitions, approvals and implementation may change; access through an API is not equivalent to licensed model export.
Overseas model hosting, access to weights and transfer of training or operations expertise may trigger distinct requirements.

paragraphs: Draft, not effective ban: The rules were under consultation through November 15. Definitions, approvals and implementation may change; access through an API is not equivalent to licensed model export.
Borderline cases: Overseas model hosting, access to weights and transfer of training or operations expertise may trigger distinct requirements.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: For any external model, distinguish API use, weight possession, fine-tuning rights and data-center deployment rights.
Keep provenance, export jurisdiction, contract permissions and fallback serving options visible before making a model a hard dependency.

paragraphs: Hosting isn't portability: For any external model, distinguish API use, weight possession, fine-tuning rights and data-center deployment rights.
Plan alternatives: Keep provenance, export jurisdiction, contract permissions and fallback serving options visible before making a model a hard dependency.
